{{2024–25 ACC men's basketball standings}}
The '''2024–25 Louisville Cardinals men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Louisville]] during the [[2024–25 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The team played its home games on Denny Crum Court at the [[KFC Yum! Center]] in [[Downtown Louisville|downtown Louisville, Kentucky]] as members of the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]] (ACC). They were led by first-year head coach [[Pat Kelsey]].

The Cardinals began their season with a victory over [[2024–25 Morehead State Eagles men's basketball team|Morehead State]] before facing twelfth-ranked [[2024–25 Tennessee Volunteers basketball team|Tennessee]]. The Volunteers defeated the Cardinals 77–55. The Cardinals won two games before traveling to [[Paradise Island|the Bahamas]] to participate in the [[Battle 4 Atlantis#2024|Battle 4 Atlantis]]. They posted an 89–61 victory in the opening game against fourteenth-ranked [[2024–25 Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball team|Indiana]] and defeated [[2024–25 West Virginia Mountaineers men's basketball team|West Virginia]] in [[Overtime (sports)#Basketball|overtime]] to reach the final. They were defeated 69–64 by [[2024–25 Oklahoma Sooners men's basketball team|Oklahoma]] to finish in second place. Upon their return home they lost two twenty third-ranked [[2024–25 Ole Miss Rebels men's basketball team|Ole Miss]] in the [[ACC–SEC Challenge]] and they lost their ACC opener against ninth-ranked [[2024–25 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|Duke]]. They rebounded with a defeat of [[2024–25 UTEP Miners men's basketball team|UTEP]] before losing to [[Kentucky–Louisville rivalry|rivals]] and fifth-ranked [[2024–25 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|Kentucky]].

The Cardinals then went on a ten-game winning streak, which included nine ACC wins. The lone non-conference victory was a three-point win over [[2024–25 Eastern Kentucky Colonels men's basketball team|Eastern Kentucky]]. Only one of the victories in this run was by less than double-digits, and that was a four-point victory at [[2024–25 Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball team|Pittsburgh]]. The streak saw the Cardinals reach twenty-first in the rankings, before a 77–70 loss at [[2024–25 Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball team|Georgia Tech]] ended the streak and their stint in the rankings. The loss was just a blip as the Cardinals went on nine-game winning streak to finish the season. The run had only one game that the Cardinals won by less than double-digits; an 89–81 victory at [[2024–25 Florida State Seminoles men's basketball team|Florida State]]. The Cardinals climbed back into the rankings on the run, finishing the regular season ranked thirteenth. They finished the regular season with wins over ACC newcomers [[2024–25 California Golden Bears men's basketball team|California]] and [[2024–25 Stanford Cardinal men's basketball team|Stanford]], defeating the latter by twenty points in their final regular season game.

The Cardinals finished the [[2024–25 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|season]] 27–8 and 18–2 in [[2024–25 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season|ACC play]] to finish in a tie for second place. As the second seed in the [[2025 ACC men's basketball tournament|2025 ACC tournament]] earned a bye into Quarterfinals where they defeated seventh seed Stanford for the second time in five days. The tournament game was much closer as the Cardinals advanced 75–73. In the Semifinals defeated third seed and tenth-ranked [[2024–25 Clemson Tigers men's basketball team|Clemson]] 76–73. The lost to first seed and top ranked Duke 73–62 in the final. They received an at-large bid to the [[2025 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA Tournament]]. The Cardinals were an eight-seed in the [[2025 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament#South regional – Atlanta, Georgia|South region]]. They lost 89–75 to nine-seed [[2024–25 Creighton Bluejays men's basketball team|Creighton]] in the First Round to end their season.

The Louisville Cardinals drew an average home attendance of 14,864, the 15th-highest of all college basketball teams.<ref>https://stats.ncaa.org/rankings/change_sport_year_div</ref>

== Previous season ==
The Cardinals began the season with a one-point win against [[2023–24 UMBC Retrievers men's basketball team|UMBC]] but lost to [[2023–24 Chattanooga Mocs men's basketball team|Chattanooga]] in their second game of the season. After defeating [[2023–24 Coppin State Eagles men's basketball team|Coppin State]], they lost both of their games in the [[Empire Classic]]. They then went on a two-game winning streak, including an overtime victory over [[2023–24 New Mexico State Aggies men's basketball team|New Mexico State]]. They went on a three-game losing streak from there, including an opening ACC game loss to [[2023–24 Virginia Tech Hokies men's basketball team|Virginia Tech]]. Their only other win in 2023 was on December 17 against [[2023–24 Pepperdine Waves men's basketball team|Pepperdine]]. The Cardinals first ACC win game at [[2023–24 Miami Hurricanes men's basketball team|Miami (FL)]] on January 10, 2024. This was [[Kenny Payne]]'s first road win as head coach.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bozich |first=Rick |date=2024-01-10 |title=BOZICH {{!}} Louisville makes major deposit, toppling Miami, 80-71, ending 22-game road losing streak |url=https://www.wdrb.com/sports/bozich-louisville-makes-major-deposit-toppling-miami-80-71-ending-22-game-road-losing-streak/article_a1b57970-b019-11ee-bd03-0337f10ff060.html |access-date=2024-04-25 |website=WDRB |language=en}}</ref> The team lost six straight games after the win. Their next wins came on February 3 and February 10, 2024, and were split by a road loss to [[2023–24 Syracuse Orange men's basketball team|Syracuse]]. The Cardinals would lose their final seven games of the ACC regular season.

The Cardinals finished the [[2023–24 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2023–24 season]] 8–24 and 3–17 in [[2023–24 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season|ACC play]] to finish in fifteenth place. As the fifteenth seed in the [[2024 ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC tournament]], they lost to tenth seed [[2023–24 NC State Wolfpack men's basketball team|NC State]] in the First Round. They were not invited to the [[2024 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] or the [[2024 National Invitation Tournament|NIT]]. After their ACC tournament loss, the Cardinals fired head coach Kenny Payne.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-03-13 |title='Change is needed': L'ville announces Payne firing |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/39723489/louisville-fires-kenny-payne-men-hoops-coach-starts-search |access-date=2024-04-25 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref>

== Offseason ==

=== Coaching changes ===
After the dismissal of head coach [[Kenny Payne]], previous [[Winthrop Eagles men's basketball|Winthrop]] and [[Charleston Cougars men's basketball|Charleston]] head coach [[Pat Kelsey]] was signed to a five-year deal as the 24th coach in Louisville's history.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Cardinals Hire Pat Kelsey to Lead Men's Basketball Program |url=https://gocards.com/news/2024/3/28/mens-basketball-cardinals-hire-pat-kelsey-to-lead-mens-basketball-program |access-date=2024-04-25 |website=University of Louisville Athletic |language=en}}</ref> Kelsey quickly brought a number of Charleston staff members to Louisville, including Brian Kloman and Thomas Carr as assistant coaches, Eli Foy as the head strength and conditioning coach, Jermaine Ukaegbu as the director of player personnel, and Mitch Johnson as the director of basketball operations. Other hires include [[LSU Tigers men's basketball|LSU's]] Ronnie Hamilton as assistant coach and retired Louisville player [[Peyton Siva]] as the director of player development/alumni relations.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Kelsey Officially Adds Kloman, Hamilton, Carr, Foy to Staff |url=https://gocards.com/news/2024/4/10/mens-basketball-kelsey-officially-adds-kloman-hamilton-carr-foy-to-staff |access-date=2024-04-25 |website=University of Louisville Athletic |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Kelsey Adds Four to Men's Basketball Staff |url=https://gocards.com/news/2024/4/16/mens-basketball-kelsey-adds-four-to-mens-basketball-staff |access-date=2024-04-25 |website=University of Louisville Athletic |language=en}}</ref>

With the additions of [[Stanford Cardinal men's basketball|Stanford]], [[California Golden Bears men's basketball|Cal]], and [[SMU Mustangs men's basketball|SMU]] the [[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]] will have a new scheduling format this season. Louisville will face [[Boston College Eagles men's basketball|Boston College]], [[Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball statistical leaders|Georgia Tech]], [[NC State Wolfpack men's basketball|NC State]], [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball|Notre Dame]], SMU, [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse]], and [[Virginia Tech Hokies men's basketball|Virginia Tech]] on the road; Cal, [[Clemson Tigers men's basketball|Clemson]], [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]], [[Miami Hurricanes men's basketball|Miami]], [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]], Stanford, and [[Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball|Wake Forest]] at home; and [[Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball|Pitt]], [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia]] and [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State]] twice for home and away games.<ref>{{Cite web |last=McGavic |first=Matthew |date=2024-02-29 |title=Louisville Men's Basketball's 2024-25 ACC Opponents Announced |url=https://www.si.com/college/louisville/basketball/2024-25-acc-opponents-revealed-mbb |access-date=2024-04-25 |website=Sports Illustrated |language=en}}</ref>
